name: BlockEditor
summary: The frame around content blocks — order, handle, removal, and the slot where your own editor goes. Aurea does not own the rich text.

a11y.apg: There is no APG pattern for drag and drop, and none for a block editor. The keyboard protocol is the one the market settled on and the one SortableList already ships — Space picks a block up, arrows move it, Space drops it, Escape puts it back — because both components share the same useReorder. Every step is announced in a polite live region. Position is not only announced: it is baked into the accessible name of the handle and the remove button, so "Reorder, Image 2 of 5" is true whenever focus lands there rather than only at the moment it changed. Dragging is never the only way.
a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 29/08/2026 (apps/keyboard-probe + tests/visual/teclado-motor.spec.ts). This ficha comes from the lineage that did not have check 30, so it declared keys with no measurement behind them — the merge of the two lineages on 29/08/2026 is what surfaced it. Confirmed: all five — Space, Enter, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Escape. Like the SortableList, the measurement had to play the protocol's first beat first: Space picks the block up, and only then do the arrows move it. The two components share the protocol — useReorder, extracted in item N1 when this became its second owner — and they now share the bank's preparation for the same reason.

props.name: blocks
props.description: The blocks, in the order they are shown. `children` is your block — a textarea, your rich text editor, a figure with a caption. `kind` names it for a screen reader ("Image", "Quote"); it falls back to a generic "Block".

props.name: onReorder
props.description: Called with the two indexes. The editor is controlled and keeps no order of its own — the keyboard path and the pointer path call this same callback, so there are never two sources of truth.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Optional. Omit it and no remove button is rendered — a button that cannot do anything is a focus target that lies to whoever uses the keyboard, which is the defect the Gallery measured in item L2.

notes: This component does NOT own the rich text. There is no bold, no italic, no bubble menu and no formatting toolbar — that engine stays with you, and ADR-0025 has the four measurements behind that decision. The most important one is security: a browser does not sanitize pasted HTML, so whoever owns the editing surface owns the XSS. Aurea cannot decide what is safe to render inside your domain.
There is no insert affordance, and that is deliberate rather than missing: adding a block is appending to your own collection, and the reorder here carries the new block to any position.
